trust_decision.summary: Whether a client-supplied sort.name may be spliced raw into ORDER BY; at the pinned commit it is decided only by a deny-list in SortRequest.getName() plus an @Pattern allow-list that is enforced only when the controller parameter has @Validated, which /account-pool/page lacks.

landing_point.why: Summary names POST /account-pool/page and sort.name; this is the only page handler that takes BasePageRequest without @Validated (the sibling CluePoolController.java:35 has it).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Adding @Validated to the one controller looks complete, since every other page handler already has it and @Pattern already exists on SortRequest.name; a solver could call the getter-level hardening redundant.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Sorting by camelCase field names (converted to snake_case by camelToUnderline and matched against per-mapper allow-lists such as 'department_id') and by numeric custom-field ids bound via #{sortName}; an over-broad fix (column allow-list in the DTO, rejecting digits, or dropping camelToUnderline) breaks these sorts.

O6_input_shapes: name with non-alphanumeric characters that evade the deny-list (now rejected by the ^[A-Za-z0-9]+$ check in the getter)

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The customer-pool twin already shipped without it; copy-paste controllers in parallel modules commonly diverge on @Validated.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A chart/statistics route whose ORDER BY or axis identifier comes from a request DTO with only the SqlInjectionChecker deny-list
